article.title: Hardly/Scarcely…when
article.part: Construcciones avanzadas y fenómenos excepcionales — Advanced constructions and exceptional phenomena
article.chapter: Combinaciones avanzadas de cláusulas — Advanced clause combinations

claims.summary: English hardly/scarcely ... when presents a second event as occurring immediately after an earlier one. When hardly or scarcely is fronted, it triggers subject–auxiliary inversion (Hardly had I arrived when ...); in ordinary medial position no such inversion occurs. Past perfect in the first clause and simple past in the when-clause are characteristic of formal retrospective narration.
